title: LicoUp extension package manifest
description: What a package says about itself before the host runs anything. It carries no artifact digest and no signature: those are produced from the bytes by packaging and by the update mechanism. `requires` is the install closure; `optionalRequires` enables extra capability only when the user already has it, and never installs anything by itself. `compatibility` is the package's own list of supported client versions: the kernel loads a package only when that list covers the running client, and `hostProtocol` is the separate wire contract range. `conversion` is the package's own claim about the persisted formats it owns: the published source formats it reads, the target format it produces and the native entry inside its payload that performs the move. It is absent from a package that owns no format, and a package that was asked for a conversion it does not declare is refused.

What a package says about itself before the host runs anything. It carries no artifact digest and no signature: those are produced from the bytes by packaging and by the update mechanism. `requires` is the install closure; `optionalRequires` enables extra capability only when the user already has it, and never installs anything by itself. `compatibility` is the package's own list of supported client versions: the kernel loads a package only when that list covers the running client, and `hostProtocol` is the separate wire contract range. `runtime.mode` is the package category: `process`, `declarative` and `service` are carried by something the host starts or bridges, while `data` is carried by nothing and contributes only the typed `resources` it declares.

id.description: The namespaced package identity, for example `org.licoland.adapter.generic`.

version.description: The package's own version. Each package version is independent of the SDK version, the host ABI, the data schemas and the renderer profile.

hostProtocol.description: The host wire protocol range this package needs. A different major refuses this package and nothing else.

compatibility.description: The client versions this package says it supports. It is not `hostProtocol`, which is the wire contract range negotiated per connection, and it is not the package's own version: a package version that differs from the client is not itself a refusal. The host admits a package at install and at activation only when this list covers the running client.

clientVersions.description: Each entry is a bare major version (`"1"`) or a semantic-version range (`">=0.3.0, <0.5.0"`). An empty list supports no client, so a package that declares none is admitted by nothing.

conversion.description: The native format conversion this package owns. The field is optional: a package that owns no persisted format carries nothing here, so an absent field is complete. A package that was asked for a conversion and declares none is refused by the caller that required it, with the package and the required source format named. The declaration names format identities, never a client version: which client builds may load the package is `compatibility`, and this field says which formats it converts. The vocabulary is the one the release index publishes for its per-package `converter` entry.

kind.description: The only converter kind this contract publishes: a program inside the package payload, run directly by its host. A converter that needs an interpreter would borrow a runtime the package does not carry, so no other kind is expressible.

sourceFormats.description: The published source formats this converter reads. An empty list converts nothing, so it is refused rather than read as `no source is supported`.

profiles.description: The narrow method profiles this package serves. A profile id this host does not publish is preserved and refused for its own operations only. A `data` package serves no profile at all: it declares resources, not a program, so its list is empty.

id.description: One of the published profiles, or an id a newer host published. An id this host does not know is preserved, refuses nothing, and grants nothing.

runtime.description: How the package is carried. A `user:` runtime reference names an interpreter or tool the user installed, which the host reuses and never removes. `data` is the category for a package the host never starts: it has no entry, no `runtimeRef`, no descriptor and no endpoint, and a data runtime that carries any other field is refused rather than read as a program.

activation.description: `on-demand` starts the package when a call needs it; `explicit` starts it only when the user asks, and is the conservative default when the field is absent. A data package is never started, so the field describes no behavior for it.

requires.description: Installed together with this package. This decides the install closure and nothing else; it does not enter a development task graph.

optionalRequires.description: Enabled when already present. Never installed on this package's account, and never a reason to refuse the package.

permissions.description: What the package asks for. A request is not a grant and there is no field here for one; the host decides, and a first install or a widened scope needs the user's consent.

contributions.description: Interface contributions, each described by a `licoup.ui-contribution.v1` resource.

resources.description: The typed data resources this package contributes. Two resources with one identity are one resource declared twice and are refused: the host compares resource identities, not whole declarations. Each declaration repeats the shape identifier its kind publishes, and no kind is free-form: the fields a declaration may carry are exactly the ones published for that kind. A package that declares one resource is a `data` package and is refused if it is also carried by a program. `definition` names a file inside the package, and a definition that is missing, absolute or outside the package is refused before publication. A composition component binds only host primitives and host actions this manifest declares in `hostPrimitives` and `hostActions`.

hostPrimitives.description: The compiled host primitives this package's resources may bind. A name this client generation does not compile is refused, and a composition component binding a primitive outside this set is refused before the package is published.

hostActions.description: The host-registered actions this package's resources may invoke, each a namespaced action identity. A composition component naming an action outside this set is refused. The declaration grants no authority: the host owns the action's effect and decides it when the action is invoked.

extensions.description: The package's own namespaced attributes. A host that does not understand one preserves it and never rules on it.

converterEntry.description: A converter entry inside the package payload: a relative path with at least one directory component and no empty, `.` or `..` segment. An entry outside the payload is not this package's entry, and the release declaration refuses the same shapes.

formatIdentity.description: A published format identity: lowercase alphanumeric words joined by `.` or `-`, such as `licoup.conversation.v1`. It is an identity rather than an ordering, and it is never a client version.

hostPrimitive.description: A host primitive compiled into this client generation. A package chooses among them; it never brings its own.

localeTag.description: A bounded locale tag: a two or three letter language subtag followed by at most three alphanumeric subtags, such as `en`, `zh-CN` or `pt-BR`.

fontFamily.description: A font family name the package covers. Leading and trailing whitespace and control characters are refused, so a name is the name the host looks up.

resourceDefinition.description: The file inside the package that carries the resource, as a relative path. The host reads it from the installed content: an absolute path, a platform separator, a parent-directory segment or a missing file is refused.

actionRef.description: The host action this component may invoke. It must be one the manifest declares in `hostActions`; the host owns the action's authority.

tokens.description: The design token identities this theme supplies.

regions.description: The client shell region identities this layout addresses.

targets.description: The visual target identities this style addresses.

families.description: The font family names the package supplies.

locales.description: The locale tags the package supplies strings for.

components.description: The components this composition binds to host primitives and host actions.

dataResource.description: One typed data resource. The `kind` decides the shape: a theme carries tokens, a layout regions, a style targets, a font families, a language locale tags and a composition components.
